rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The awakening means that God roused them and stirred them from sleep.
rows.anchor: أي أيقظناهم وأثرناهم من نومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first party may be those who said they stayed a day or part of one, and the second those who said God knew best.
rows.anchor: أي منهم وهم القائلون ولبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم والقائلون

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says most commentators identify the two parties as the youths who guessed briefly and the people of the city, who knew their absence's duration from records.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن عطية أن هذا قول جمهور المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the parties as the sleepers and the successive kings who ruled the city.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن أحد الحزبين الفتية والآخر الملوك الذين تداولوا ملك المدينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the two parties were believers and unbelievers among the people of the cave.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : الحزبان قوم أهل الكهف حزب منهم مؤمنون وحزب كافرون

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says both parties were believers living in the same era who disagreed about how long the sleepers remained.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : الحزبان مؤمنان كانوا في زمنهم واختلفوا في مدة لبثهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies both parties as unbelievers: Jews and Christians who informed Quraysh about asking the Prophet concerning the cave.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : الحزبان كافران والمراد بهما اليهود والنصارى الذين علموا قريشا

rows.speaker: ابن حرب
rows.claim: Ibn Harb identifies the two parties as God and creation, invoking the question, “Are you more knowing, or God?”
rows.anchor: وقال ابن حرب : الحزبان الله سبحانه وتعالى والخلق كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the parties already mentioned in the exchange, since the definite article points back to them and supplies no other antecedent.
rows.anchor: هو الأول لأن اللام للعهد ولا عهد لغير من سمعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads ahsa as a past-tense verb meaning “measured precisely,” with ay as its subject; al-Farisi, al-Zamakhshari, and Ibn Atiyya choose this too.
rows.anchor: فهو فعل ماض وفاعله ضمير ( أي ) واختار ذلك الفارسي والزمخشري وابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred parsing, ma is a verbal noun, the prepositional phrase is an advanced circumstantial phrase, and amadan is the object of ahsa.
rows.anchor: وما في قوله تعالى : ( ( لما لبثوا ( مصدرية والجار والمجرور حال مقدم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines amad as a bounded period; unlike zaman, it is considered with regard to its endpoint, while another lexicographer says amad and mada are close.
rows.anchor: والأمد على ما قال الراغب : مدة لها حد والفرق بينه وبين الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question concerns counting the duration as discrete units, dividing it into years and reaching a numerical count, not measuring its continuous extent.
rows.anchor: والمراد من إحصائها ضبطها من حيث كميتها المنفصلة العارضة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes amad as the duration's endpoint: the count may concern the full 309 years or the final, three-hundred-ninth year, with the latter counting the number's encompassed ranks.
rows.anchor: أن ما تعلق به الإحصاء في الصورة السابقة نفس المدة المنقمسة إلى السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take amad literally as the duration and figuratively as its endpoint; either sense can be defended by construing the duration as an ongoing state with a limit.
rows.anchor: وقيل إطلاق الأمد على المدة مجاز وحقيقته غاية المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raghib's clear lexical usage makes duration the literal sense of amad and endpoint figurative; forcing the endpoint reading is unnecessary when ma is verbal.
rows.anchor: ظاهر كلام الراغب وهو هو في اللغة يقتضي أن الأمد حقيقة في المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ma is a relative pronoun instead, its omitted relative pronoun means “the time in which they stayed.”
rows.anchor: نعم يحتاج إليه على تقدير جعلها موصولة حذف عائدها من الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed purpose-clause reading of ma, with the lam added because the clause is neither a verbal noun nor simultaneous, is weak.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما لبثوا في موضع المفعول له وجيء بلام التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes lam extra and ma a relative object, with amadan an accusative specification transferred from the object: originally, “count the duration of their time.”
rows.anchor: وقيل اللام مزيدة وما موصولة وهي المفعول به وعائدها محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that a specification must derive from a subject is unfounded: recognized grammars allow it to derive from an object, as in the earth being made to burst into springs.
rows.anchor: لأن اللابدية في حيز المنع والذي تحقق في المعتبرات كشروح التسهيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A specification of relation is not a specification of an individual noun, and grammarians do not require the latter to be transformed from a subject.
rows.anchor: ولو جعل تمييزا لما كان تمييزا لمفرد ولم يقل أحد باشتراط التحويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allowing ma to be verbal under the preceding analysis is possible but remote; adding lam is also weak because it is not added in such a construction.
rows.anchor: وجوز في ما على هذا التقدير أن تكون مصدرية وهو بعيد وضعف القول بزيادة اللام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Tabrizi read ahsa as a comparative, supported by comparable Qur’anic comparisons and their view that awakening cannot aim at a count completed before it.
rows.anchor: واختار الزجاج والتبريزي كون ( أحصى ) أفعل تفضيل لأنه الموافق لما وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One objection is that comparatives from non-triliteral verbs are not regular; grammarians variously allow them, forbid them except as anomalies, or allow them when the hamza is not causative.
rows.anchor: بأن بناء أفعل التفضيل من غير الثلاثي المجرد ليس بقياس

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh apparently permits forming a comparative from non-triliteral verbs without restriction.
rows.anchor: الجواز مطلقا وهو ظاهر كلام سيبويه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali forbids such formation except for anomalous forms, which cannot serve as a productive pattern.
rows.anchor: والمنع مطلقا وما ورد شاذ لا يقاس عليه وهو مذهب أبي علي

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn Asfur distinguishes causative hamza, which blocks comparative formation, from other hamza; here the hamza is not causative.
rows.anchor: والتفصيل بين أن تكون الهمزة للنقل فلا يجوز لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection asks how the comparative can govern amadan as a direct object; supplying an omitted verb merely repeats the text, while other parses distort the sense.
rows.anchor: بأن ( أمدا ) حينئذ إن نصب على أنه مفعول به

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan treats amadan as a duration governed by a dropped preposition: the original would mean “for a duration”; ma explicates an otherwise vague word.
rows.anchor: ووجه أبو حيان نصبه بأن على إسقاط حرف الجر وهو بمعنى المدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that a comparative cannot take a direct object reflects Basran grammar, not Kufan grammar; nevertheless the proposed reading makes amadan a specification, which comparatives can govern.
rows.anchor: وتعقب منع صلاحية أفعل لنصب المفعول به بأنه قول البصريين دون الكوفيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A past-tense verb does not imply knowledge of the count before awakening; the past reflects the time of narration.
rows.anchor: بأن صيغة الماضي باعتبار حال الحكاية ولا يكاد يتوهم من ذلك الإشعار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final objection says the comparative implies both parties had counted and one was simply more accurate, though the story shows otherwise.
rows.anchor: بأنه يلزم حينئذ أن يكون أصل الإحصاء متحققا في الحزبين إلا أن بعضهم

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says al-Zajjaj's view is not so objectionable, but al-Zamakhshari's preferred reading is better in wording and meaning because the parties were discussing, not ranking expertise.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف أن قول الزجاج ليس بذلك المردود إلا أن ما آثره الزمخشري أحق بالإيثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ay is an interrogative subject followed by its predicate; in this construction it suspends the verb naʿlam from taking its normal object.
rows.anchor: وأي استفهامية مبتدأ وما بعدها خبرها وقد علقت نعلم عن العمل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: If ahsa is a comparative, ay may be a relative pronoun built as a noun of relation because its relative clause has its opening pronoun omitted; it cannot be built that way with a finite verb.
rows.anchor: جاز أن تكون أي موصولا مبنيا على مذهب سيبويه لوجود شرط جواز البناء

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reads liyaʿlama with a yāʾ, shifting the attribution of the action to God in a grammatical turn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري ( ليعلم ) بالياء على إسناد الفعل إليه تعالى بطريق الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge as the aim of awakening is not literal, which would imply the false claim attributed to Hisham.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك على ظاهره وإلا تكن الآية دليلا لهشام على ما يزعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation reads “know” as a metaphor for making the truth manifest or distinguishing the parties; another makes divine knowledge newly related to an event after it occurs.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو غاية بجعله مجازا عن الإظهار والتمييز وقيل : المراد ليتعلق علمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second explanation is compared to testing who follows the Messenger and who turns back after the change of prayer direction.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : ( لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب عى عقبيه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A critic objects that awakening did not divide the parties into accurate counters and non-counters, unlike the changed prayer direction, which separated followers from deserters.
rows.anchor: بأن بعث هؤلاء الفئة لم يترتب عليه تفرقهم إلى المحصي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The critic instead treats the wording as a test: God exposes their inability to know the duration, so they defer to Him, gain certainty in resurrection, and become a sign to believers and deniers.
rows.anchor: إن جعل ذلك غاية بحمل النظم الكريم على التنفيذ المبني على جعل العلم عبارة عن الاختبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects portraying God as awakening them like someone who wants to discover an unknown result, since that might suggest desire necessitates fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وهذا أولى من تصوير التمثيل بأن يقال بعثناهم بعث من يريد أن يعلم

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says a real test is impossible for an all-knowing God and that calling it a metaphor returns to the rejected claim; he reads knowledge as a metonym for public manifestation.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه الخفاجي بأن ما ذكره مع تكلفه وقلة جدواه غير مستقيم

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: On al-Khafaji's reading, revelation makes the sleepers' case visible, reassuring believers and cutting off deniers' arguments; the wording points to the implication of knowledge suited to context.
rows.anchor: واختار جعل العلم كناية عن ظهور أمرهم ليطمئن بازدياد الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duration dispute is singled out because disagreement over it gives the story stronger public visibility and wider circulation.
rows.anchor: وإنما علق العلم بالإختلاف في أمده أي المفهوم من أي الحزبين أحصى

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf explains knowledge as figurative distinction and disclosure: the people who know the duration are exposed, though neither party actually did so.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف توجيها لما في الكشاف أراد أن العلم مجاز عن التمييز والإظهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds al-Kashf's explanation less costly than al-Khafaji's and prefers the test-like illustration; the worry about implying divine desire is negligible.
rows.anchor: وما في الكشف أقل مؤنة منه وتصوير التمثيل بأن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the active reading liyaʿlama, God is the subject and an object is omitted; the following clause supplies two objects, or one if knowledge means recognition.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( ليعلم ) مبنيا للفاعل من الإعلام وخرج ذلك على أن الفاعل ضميره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading liyaʿlama omits its deputy subject; the following clause may supply the objects or the single object according to the sense of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( ليعلم ) بالبناء للمفعول وخرج على أن نائب الفاعل محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Kufans allow the following clause itself to function as the deputy subject; Basrans forbid clauses as subjects or deputy subjects, while Kufans differ about the condition for allowing it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أن الجملة هي النائب عن الفاعل وهو مذهب كوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage begins unpacking the story previously summarized: God now recounts its significant details to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: شروع في تفصيل ما أجمل فيما سلف أي نحن نخبرك بتفصيل خبرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-haqq may modify an omitted verbal noun, function circumstantially for the subject of “We recount,” or qualify their report circumstantially.
rows.anchor: إما صفة لمصدر محذوف أو حال من ضمير ( نقص ) أو ( من نبأهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse makes al-haqq qualify nabāʾ by omitting a relative pronoun, for grammarians who allow deleting it with part of its clause.
rows.anchor: أو صفة له على رأي من يرى جواز حذف الموصول مع بعض الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests that “with truth” may allude to people in the Prophet's time recounting their story inaccurately.
rows.anchor: ولعل في التقليد ( بالحق ) إشارة إلى أن في عهده صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf cites Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt to argue that Arabs knew of the cave story, though they did not know it accurately.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف بعد نقل شعر أمية بن أبي الصلت السابق

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others describe Christians whose community had become sinful and idolatrous under tyrants, while a remnant still followed Jesus and worshipped one God.
rows.anchor: حسبما ذكره ابن إسحاق وغيره أنه مرج أهل الإنجيل وعظمت فيهم الخطايا

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: The king called Daqyanus or Daqyus persecuted Christians, offering death or idol worship and displaying the bodies of believers he killed.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية دقيوس فإنه غلا غلوا شديدا فجاس خلال الديار والبلاد

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: The youths were prominent residents of Ephesus or Tarsus; they were arrested while praying, confessed one God before the king, and their eldest, Mکسlimina, spoke first.
rows.anchor: واسمها على ما في بعض الروايات إفسوس وفي بعضها طرسوس

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: The king stripped their fine clothes and delayed punishment because they were young, giving them time to reconsider while he left for Nineveh.
rows.anchor: فأمر الجبار فنزع ما عليهم من الثياب الفاخرة وأخرجهم من عنده

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: After agreeing to flee, each youth took money from his family, gave some away, and carried the rest to a nearby cave called Banjalus.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أن يأخذ كل منهم نفقة من بيت أبيه فيتصدق ببعضها ويتزود بالباقي

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: They prayed and fasted in the cave; Yumlikha secretly bought supplies and gathered news until the returning king sought them, after which they prostrated and fell asleep with their dog.
rows.anchor: فلبثوا فيه ليس لهم عمل إلا الصلاة والصيام والتسبيح والتحميد

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: When the king could not enter the cave, an adviser proposed walling it up so the youths would die of hunger and thirst, and the king did so.
rows.anchor: فابن عليهم باب الكهف ودعهم يموتوا جوعا وعطشا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the youths met by chance while fleeing an idol-worshipping king, concealed their reasons, pledged to share them, then united in confessing God and entered the cave.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Their families searched after they disappeared; the king ordered their names written on a lead tablet kept in his treasury.
rows.anchor: فدعا بلوح من رصاص فكتب فيه أسماءهم ثم طرح في خزانته

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says the youths worked as money changers.
rows.anchor: وكانوا على ما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي جعفر صيارفة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih recounts a follower of Jesus who avoided a city's gate idol, worked in a bathhouse, and brought selected youths to faith through teaching about heaven and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وابن المنذر عن وهب بن منبه قال : جاء رجل من حواري عيسى

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: In Wahb's account, the ruler's son died in the bathhouse with a woman after being rebuked; the converts fled with a fellow farmer, slept in a cave, and were walled in when the king's men could not enter.
rows.anchor: فمروا بصاحب لهم في زرع له وهو على مثل أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narratives differ, and no sound hadith explains how the youths met or left; the account to rely on is the Quranic description.
rows.anchor: في الحديث الصحيح كيفية اجتماعهم وخروجهم ولا معول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They were youths” resumes the story as an answer to an implied question and echoes the earlier discussion of the word futiyya.
rows.anchor: استئناف مبني على السؤال من قبل المخاطب وتقدم الكلام آنفا في الفتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their faith in their Lord means faith in their master and guardian; the shift to third person highlights that lordship caused their belief and later declaration.
rows.anchor: أي بسيدهم والناظر في مصالحهم وفيه التفات من التكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their guidance increased through steadfastness in faith, success in righteous action, turning wholly to God, and asceticism toward worldly life.
rows.anchor: بالتثبيت على الإيمان والتوفيق للعمل الصالح والإنقطاع إلى الله تعالى والزهد

rows.speaker: التحرير
rows.claim: Al-Tahrir gives two interpretations of the increase: the fruits of guidance or increased certainty.
rows.anchor: وفي التحرير المراد زدناهم ثمرات هدى أو يقينا قولان

rows.speaker: التحرير
rows.claim: Al-Tahrir says the increase came either through obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions or through the dog affirming their faith, an angel's reassurance, and news of an Arab prophet whose mission they accepted before his call.
rows.anchor: وما حصلت به الزيادة امتثال المأمور وترك المنهي أو انطاق الكلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An angel's reported visit does not entail that the youths were prophets.
rows.anchor: ولا يلزم من القول بإنزال ملك عليهم بذلك القول بنبوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “We increased” shifts from third to first person, magnifying the importance of the increase.
rows.anchor: وفي ( زدناهم ) التفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم الذي عليه سبك النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God steadied their hearts with patience so separation from home, family, comfort, friends, the tyrant, and the crowd of unbelievers would not shake them.
rows.anchor: قويناها بالصبر فلم تزحزحها عواصف فراق الأوطان وترك الأهل والنعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Binding” the heart is metaphorical; lexicons use binding for fastening an animal and figuratively for giving someone patience and steadfast resolve.
rows.anchor: وأصل الربط الشد المعروف واستعماله فيما ذكر مجاز

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf explains the metaphor by contrasting panic that makes hearts rise to the throats with a heart made firm and settled.
rows.anchor: لما كان الخوف والتعلق يزعج القلوب عن مقارها ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some analyze the phrase as an implicit metaphor made vivid, with ʿala used despite the verb's usual direct-object construction.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يكون في الكلام استعارة مكنية تخييلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “standing” means resolutely setting out toward God and opposing their people, like the idiom “so-and-so undertook” an action; it may also mean standing to proclaim religion.
rows.anchor: والمراد بقيامهم انبعاثهم بالعزم على التوجه إلى الله تعالى ومنابذة الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says they left the city, met by chance, and one voiced his conviction that his Lord was Lord of heaven and earth, which the others shared.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم أنهم خرجوا من المدينة واجتمعوا وراءها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's account has them first concealing their intentions, then making a pledge before agreeing on their shared confession.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه قال : إن بعضهم أخفى حاله عن بعض حتى تعاهدوا

rows.speaker: صاحب الغنيان
rows.claim: The Ghunyān says they stood before King Daqyanus; a cat or mouse frightened him, and the youths blurted out their confession without fear.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الغنيان المراد به وقوفهم بين يدي الجبار دقيانوس

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says their standing was rising from sleep, but the author dismisses this and the similar claim that it means remaining firm in faith.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء : المراد قيامهم من النوم وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's lordship over heaven and earth entails lordship over everything in them, including the youths, so they begin with that premise and then reject every other deity.
rows.anchor: فإن ربوبيته تعالى للسموات والأرض تقتضي ربوبيته لما فيها وهم من جملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They use lan because it is more emphatic than other negators and may cover all time: they will never worship another deity, alone or alongside God.
rows.anchor: وجاءوا بلن لأن النفي بها أبلغ من النفي بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say ilah rather than rabb to reject their opponents' naming idols as gods and to identify divinity as the basis of worship; the phrases can also express distinct lordship and worship monotheisms.
rows.anchor: وعدلوا عن قولهم ربا إلى قولهم ( إلها ) للتنصيص على رد المخالفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters acknowledge God's lordship as creator but deny exclusive worship, claiming idols bring them nearer to God and reciting a formula that gives Him a partner He owns.
rows.anchor: وحكى سبحانه عنهم أنهم يقولون : ( إنما نعبدهم ليقربون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths state lordship first as the first rank of monotheism and a gradual challenge: exclusive lordship entails exclusive divinity, which God argues against polytheists elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وابتدأوا بما يشير إلى توحيد الربوبية لأنه أول مراتب التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the first clause itself to indicate exclusive worship, making the second clause reinforce it.
rows.anchor: ولكون الجملة الأولى مشيرة إلى توحيد الألوهية قيل أن في الجملة الثانية تأكيدا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from apart from Him” modifies the following indefinite noun in a circumstantial construction, or qualifies it if placed after the noun.
rows.anchor: والجار والمجرور متعلق بحدوث وقع حالا من النكرة بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatatan means a statement far from truth, either a verbal noun or a source used adjectivally for emphatic effect.
rows.anchor: أي قولا ذا شططا أي بعد عن الحق مفرد أو قولا هو عين الشطط

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa permits shatatan as the direct object of “we said.”
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء كون ( شططا ( مفعولا به لقلنا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses shatatan as a lie; Ibn Zayd says error and al-Suddi says injustice, all derivative senses of excessive distance from truth.
rows.anchor: وفسره قتادة بالكذب وابن زيد بالخطأ والسدي بالجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root shatta denotes moving too far away, as illustrated by a cited line of poetry.
rows.anchor: وأصل معناه ما أشرنا إليه لأنه من شط إذا أفرط في البعد وأنشدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted oath is answered by the emphatic lam; idha is conditional or responsive, with the implied condition that invoking another god would be an outrageous statement.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام قسم مقدر واللام واقعة في جوابه ( وإذا ( حرف جواب وجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship necessarily entails acknowledging and petitioning a deity, so the speech implies that the youths were urged to worship idols and reproached for refusing, consistent with their standing before the king.
rows.anchor: واستلزم العبادة القول لما أنها لا تعرى عن الاعتراف بألوهية المعبود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their advice is to withdraw from the people and their worship, then worship God alone somewhere safe; its fulfillment confirms their sincerity and the preceding counsel.
rows.anchor: وإذا اجتنبتم عنهم وعما يعبدون فأخلصوا له العبادة في موضع تتمكنون منه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra takes faʾwu as the answer to idha; another analysis makes it evidence of an implied answer: first separate inwardly, then physically if needed.
rows.anchor: وإلى كون ( فأووا ( جواب إذ ذهب الفراء وقيل إنه دليل الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both conditional analyses are challenged because idha without ma is not conditional; the claim that it can be conditional is weak or merely semantic shorthand.
rows.anchor: واعترض كلا القولين بأن إذ بدون ما لا تكون للشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accordingly, idha is causal or temporal, attached either to an implied command or to the stated command; Abu al-Baqa attaches it to an implied “they said to one another,” which the author calls astonishing.
rows.anchor: فهي هنا تعليلية أو ظرفية وتعلقها قيل بأووا محذوفا دل عليه المذكور

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A report from Qatada gives Ibn Masud's codex the explanatory wording “what they worship besides God”; Harun reports “besides us” in another codex.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود كما أخرج ابن جريج وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: في البحر
rows.claim: The codex variants are explanatory glosses, not readings, because they conflict with the Uthmanic consonantal text.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أن المصحفين تفسير لا قراءة لمخالفته سواد الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanshur means to spread and expand; rabb is the guardian who guided them to faith; mercy covers both worlds; yuhayyiʾ means to make easy, and the omitted object is good or similar benefit.
rows.anchor: يبسط لكم ويوسع عليكم ( ﴿ ربكم ﴾ مالك أمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min amrikum may attach to yuhayyiʾ as source or partitive, or, according to Ibn al-Anbari, mean God will replace their hard situation with a refuge.
rows.anchor: على ما في بعض الحواشي متعلق بيهيء ومن الابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reads min as substitution: God prepares a refuge in place of their difficult circumstances, as in the cited verse and a poem wishing for Zamzam water.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : للبدل والمعنى يهييء لكم بدلا عن أمركم الصعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min amrikum may alternatively be an implied circumstantial phrase modifying marfiqan.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون حالا من ( مرفقا ) فيتعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting lakum first signals early that the following provision benefits them and builds anticipation; their statement reflects trust, hope, and certainty in God.
rows.anchor: وتقديم ( لكم ) لما مر مرارا من الايذان من أول الأمر بكون المؤخر من منافعهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every prophet was sent as a young man and every scholar received knowledge while young, citing Abraham, Moses, and the cave youths.
rows.anchor: أخرج الطبراني وابن المنذر عن ابن عباس قال : ما بعث الله تعالى نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possibilities that a contemporary prophet told the youths their refuge would be prepared, or that one of them was a prophet receiving revelation, are unsupported conjecture.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن ما ذكر مجرد احتمال من غير داع

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, Humayd, Ibn Saʿdan, Nafiʿ, Ibn Amir, and others read marfiqan with mīm open and faʾ kasra; another reading reverses the vowels.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والأعرج وشيبة وحميد وابن سعدان ونافع وابن عامر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Thaʿlab say both vowel patterns mean either something useful or the bodily joint.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق بينه وبين ما هو بكسر الميم وفتح الفاء معنى على ما حكاه الزجاج وثعلب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says he knows only kasra for a useful object or the elbow; al-Kisai says the elbow alone takes the open-mim form, which Abu Hatim disputes as meaning a place.
rows.anchor: ونقل مكي عن الفراء أنه قال : لا أعرف في الأمر وفي اليد وفي كل شيء إلا كسر الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other authorities call the two forms dialect variants for a useful thing, while distinguishing the elbow's form; Hejaz speakers and other Arabs differ, and Muadh permits both vowels open.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما لغتان فيما يرتفق به وأما من اليد فبكسر الميم وفتح الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports migration to preserve religion and condemns remaining in an unbelieving land when remaining requires professing disbelief.
rows.anchor: هذا واستدل بالآية على حسن الهجرة لسلامة الدين وقبح المقام في دار الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's movement describes the youths after they entered the cave, inferred from the earlier mention of their taking refuge and the cave being theirs; other narrative details are also omitted.
rows.anchor: بيان لحالهم بعد ما أووا إلى الكهف ولم يصرح سبحانه به تعويلا على ما سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omission may also signal that their following wise advice was obvious; the address is to the Prophet or any suitable observer and emphasizes visibility rather than an actual sighting.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو لكل أحد ممن يصلح له

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufan and several other readers pronounce tazāwar with two original tāʾs, deleting one for ease.
rows.anchor: وأصله تتزاور بتاءين فحذف أحدهما تخفيفا وهي قراءة الكوفيين والأعمش

rows.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Harami readers and Abu Amr read tazāwar with an open tāʾ and geminated zāy, assimilating the first tāʾ after it changes to zāy.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وأبو عمرو ( تزاور ) بفتح التاء وتشديد الزاي

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وابن عامر وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Amir, Qatada, Humayd, and others read tazawwar, a rare verb form outside the usual defect and color meanings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن إسحاق وابن عامر وقتادة وحميد ويعقوب عن العمري ( تزور

rows.speaker: جابر والجحدري وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: Jabir, al-Jahdari, Abu Rajaʾ, and others read tazwār, another rare derived form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جابر والجحدري وأبو رجاء والسختياني وابن أبي عبلة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and Abu al-Mutawakkil read tazwāʾr, inserting a hamza to avoid two adjacent still letters.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبو المتوكل ( تزوئر ) بهمزة قبل الراء المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these readings derive from zawr, meaning inclination or deviation; its scope is general, though some restrict it to a natural inclination, and poets use the root of bodily leaning.
rows.anchor: وكلها من الزور بفتحتين مع التخفيف وهو الميل وقيده بعضهم بالخلقى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib links zawr to the upper chest and says azwar is one whose chest inclines; visiting someone can mean turning one's chest toward him, though the author favors the common derivation.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : إن الزور بتحريك الواو ميل في الزور بتسكينها وهو أعلى الصدر

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan claims the verse's verb has no meaning here because azwar means contraction; the author calls this an attack on Ibn Amir's reading that distorts his attribution.
rows.anchor: وحكى عن أبي الحسن أنه قال : لا معنى لتزور في الآية لأن الأزوار الانقباض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun turns away from their cave; idafa to them is by loose association, and dhat al-yamin means the cave's right side when entering or the youths' right, a locative phrase.
rows.anchor: الذي آووا إليه فالإضافة لأدنى ملابسة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says dhat al-yamin and dhat al-shimal are flexible adverbial expressions, like yamina and shimala.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد : في المقتضب ذات اليمين وذات الشمال من الظروف المتصرفة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai says qarada a place means to turn away from it without coming near.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي : يقال قرضت المكان إذا عدلت عنه ولم تقر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhat al-shimal is the cave's left side, toward the east; other authorities derive the verb from “cutting” and understand the sun as passing beyond the sleepers.
rows.anchor: أي جهة ذات شمال الكهف أي جانبه الذي يلي المشرق وقال غير واحد : هو من القرض

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line witnesses qarada in the sense of cutting through or across a place.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة : إلى طعن يقرضن أقواز مشرف شمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths lay in a broad part of the cave; the word faja is also used for space between the thighs and has several plural forms.
rows.anchor: أي في متسع من الكهف وهي على ما قيل من الفجا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم وابن عطية
rows.claim: One explanation says the cave's orientation made sunlight strike the sides to refresh the air without touching the sleepers: its entrance faced the Pleiades, and the sun's seasonal path passed beside it.
rows.anchor: لأن باب الكهف كما قال عبد الله بن مسلم وابن عطية كان في مقابلة بنات نعش

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the geometry and says God miraculously diverted the sun so it never struck them, as a sign of power and honor for the faithful.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : ليس ذلك لما ذكر بل لمحض صرف الله تعالى الشمس بيد قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors miraculous shielding: the phrase “that is among God's signs” supports it more clearly and shows divine power, true monotheism, and honor for the faithful.
rows.anchor: واحتج عليه بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali reads qarada as lending them some sunlight temporarily and quickly taking it back, so the sun misses them in the morning but lightly touches them in the evening.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي : معنى تقرضهم تعطيهم من ضوئها شيئا ثم تزول سريعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that the triliteral verb qaraḍa with that meaning is unattested, so the proposed morphology has no basis.
rows.anchor: ورد بأنه لم يسمع للقرض بهذا المعنى فعل ثلاثي ليفتح حرف المضارعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some instead take qarada as cutting light off for them, supplying an omitted laam; this was motivated by fear that total shade would spoil the air, but most commentators say sunlight never touched them.
rows.anchor: واختار بعضهم كون المراد ما ذكر إلا أنه جعل تقرضهم من القرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group also prefers God's miraculous shielding, which the demonstrative supports; extraordinary preservation is apt in a story already full of wonders.
rows.anchor: واختار جمع أنه لمحض حجب الله تعالى الشمس على خلاف ما جرت به العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take “that” to refer to the cave's orientation; others refer it to God's preserving the youths for so long or revealing their story to the Prophet, though narrative placement weakens the latter two.
rows.anchor: وبعض من ذهب إلى أن المنشأ كون باب الكهف في مقابلة بنات نعش جعل ذلك إشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author leans toward reading “that” as their guidance to monotheism, defiance of family and people despite youth, and refuge in this unusual cave.
rows.anchor: وجعله بعضهم إشارة إلى هدايتهم إلى التوحيد ومخالفتهم قومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has yaqriḍuhum with a final yāʾ; the pronoun may refer to the sun's setting.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( يقرضهم ) بالياء ءاخر الحروف ولعل الضمير عائد على غروب الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the cave is the subject of the verb: it shelters or cuts the sleepers off from the sun.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : أي يقرضهم الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whomever God guides, He directs along the path to truth and enables to do what He loves and approves.
rows.anchor: ويوفقه لمل يحبه ويرضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “he is rightly guided” either praises the youths and confirms their hoped-for refuge, or warns that only those God enables will reflect on such signs; “whoever” may include them or everyone.
rows.anchor: والمراد إما الثناء على أصحاب الكهف والشهادة لهم بإصابة المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some make the guidance phrase praise God, linking it with the previous mention of increased guidance and strengthened hearts, and take misguidance as God creating error when a person turns to it.
rows.anchor: وجعله بعضهم ثناء على الله تعالى لمناسبة قوله سبحانه ( وزدناهم هدى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the God-praise reading does not fit the context; the contrast also reinforces praise of the youths as people whose guide is a true guide, and may involve rhetorical omission.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يطابق المقام والمقابلة لا تنافي المدح بل تؤكده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The default hasabtum has an open sīn; Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and al-Kisai read it with kasra, meaning “you think,” as in the earlier address.
rows.anchor: بفتح السين وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي بكسرها أي تظنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement may be a fresh report, or it may omit “if you saw them,” yielding “you would think them awake.”
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا إخبار مستأنف وليس على تقدير شيء وقيل في الكلام حذف

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf parses ayqazan as the plural of yaqiz, with either kasra or damma on qaf, comparing each form to its corresponding plural pattern.
rows.anchor: جمع يقض بكسر القاف كإنكاد ونكد كما في الكشف وبضمها كأعضاد وعضد

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The Qamus records both qaf vowels in yaqiz and yaqizān; open eyes create the main impression of wakefulness.
rows.anchor: وفي القاموس رجل يقض كندس وكتف فحكى اللغتين ضم العين وكسرها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says an observer might infer wakefulness from their preserved appearance and lack of normal sleeping slackness even with closed eyes; reliably established open eyes would make the impression clearer.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : يحتمل أن يحسب الرائي ذلك لشدة الحفظ الذي كان عليهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says frequent turning explains why they seemed awake, but the author objects that this does not fit the explicit statement that they were asleep.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : مداره كثرة تقلبهم واستدل عليه بذكر ذلك بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some see the contrast between deep sleep and repeated turning as a display of divine power, but the author considers this unlikely because deep sleep ordinarily has little movement.
rows.anchor: وقيل يحتمل أن يكون ذلك إظاهرا لعظيم قدرته تعالى في شأنهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says they were turned once every six months; Abu Iyad gives a similar report.
rows.anchor: في أوقات تقليبهم فأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts say they were turned once a year on Ashura, only during the extra nine years, or annually during the first three hundred years but not the additional nine.
rows.anchor: وقيل يقلبون في كل سنة مرة وذلك يوم عاشوراء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the turning occurred only in the nine-year addition, not during the preceding period.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد أن التقليب في التسع سنين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they were turned annually during the first three hundred years, but not in the second sleep of nine years.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة أن هذا التقليب في رقدتهم الأولى

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says such timetables cannot be inferred by reason or the Quran and lack an authentic report; the imperfect, intensified verb instead suggests repeated turning.
rows.anchor: وتعقب الإمام ذلك بأن هذه التقديرات لا سبيل للعقل إليها

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi suggests the turning clause is circumstantial based on al-Zajjaj's explanation, but the author finds that analysis unconvincing.
rows.anchor: وجوز الطيبي بناء على ما سمعت عن الزجاج كون الجملة في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings include yuqallibuhum with yāʾ, whose subject may be God or an angel; al-Hasan also has a lighter form, while Ibn Jinni reports the verbal-noun reading taqallubahum.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( ويقلبهم ) بالياء آخر الحروف مع التشديد والضمير لله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni parses taqallubahum as an accusative verbal noun governed by an omitted “you see,” or as an initial noun with a following predicate; Ikrima reads a light verb addressed to the observer.
rows.anchor: ووجهه أنه مفعول لفعل محذوف يدل عليه ( وتحسبهم ) أي وترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalbahum most naturally means their actual dog, which has many names and inspired a separate treatise by al-Suyuti.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه الحيوان المعروف النباح وله أسماء كثيرة

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Kaʿb says a dog followed them after they repeatedly drove it away; it reassured them that it loved God's beloved and would guard them.
rows.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار : هو كلب مروا به فتبعهم فطردوه فعاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it was a shepherd's dog that followed its owner, who had joined the youths' faith.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كلب راع مروا به فتبع دينهم

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says it was either one youth's hunting dog or a sheep dog; keeping a dog for hunting or livestock is permitted, unlike other purposes.
rows.anchor: وقال عبيد بن عمير : هو كلب صيد أحدهم وقيل : كلب غنمه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A hadith in al-Bukhari from Ibn Umar says keeping a dog outside hunting or livestock reduces one's deeds daily by two qirats, or one in another narration.
rows.anchor: ففي البخاري عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما من اقتنى كلبا ليس بكلب صيد

rows.speaker: عبيد
rows.claim: A report from Ubayd says the dog was red like an embroidered cloak; another from Kathir al-Nawwa says yellow, while other accounts say it was spotted.
rows.anchor: فأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق سفيان قال : قال لي رجل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan calls the dog Qitmir; Mujahid calls it Qitmur, while other reports name it Rayyan or Thawr.
rows.anchor: وفي اسمه فأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الحسن أنه قطمير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it was larger than a Qalti and smaller than a Kurdish dog.
rows.anchor: وهو في الكبر على ما روي عن ابن عباس فوق القلطي ودون الكردي

rows.speaker: عبيد
rows.claim: Ubayd reportedly saw the dog as a small “Zini” animal, which al-Suyuti explains as Chinese; al-Khazini likewise interprets the Qalti as Chinese.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عبيد أنه قال رأيته صغيرا زينيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say kalb means lion, a possible dictionary sense; a Prophetic supplication against an unbeliever was fulfilled by a lion, but that does not fit the verse's plain wording.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المراد بالكلب هنا الأسد وهو على ما في القاموس أحد معانيه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj asked a learned man whether the dog was a lion; the man swore it was a red dog called Qitmura.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج أنه قال : قلت لرجل من أهل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More remote claims identify the dog as a human cook or attendant, or one of the youths stationed as a lookout.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من هذا زعم من ذهب إلى أنه رجل طباخ لهم تبعهم أو أحدهم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الزاهدي
rows.claim: Abu Amr al-Zahidi records a reading kalibahum with hamza and alif from “to guard,” which could mean a human sentinel; the canonical reading still points to a dog.
rows.anchor: نعم حكى أبو عمرو الزاهدي غلام ثعلب أنه قريء ( وكالبهم ) بهمزة مضمومة

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq reads kalibahum with a doubled noun pattern, meaning the owner of their dog, like someone described as owning milk or dates.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه ( وكالبهم ) بباء موحدة وزنة اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: خالد بن معدان
rows.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan says the only beasts in Paradise are the cave dog and Balaam's donkey; other lists include Salih's camel and Ishmael's ram but lack reliable support.
rows.anchor: فعن خالد بن معدان ليس في الجنة من الدواب إلا كلب أصحاب الكهف وحمار بلعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account understood from al-Tirmidhi's wording appears to affirm horses in Paradise, while claims about other animals have no report one can rely on.
rows.anchor: نعم في الجنة حيوانات مخلوقة فيها وفي خبر يفهم من كلام الترمذي صحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Shiʿites name sons “Dog of Ali” and hope for salvation by analogy; a popular poem celebrates the cave dog and dog of Ali, which the author answers with a joke about Ali's own dog.
rows.anchor: حتى أن بعض الشيعة يسمون أبناءهم بكلب علي ويؤمل من سمى بذلك النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basit dhiraʿayhi means stretching the two forelegs; the participle governs its object because the narration depicts a past scene, or because some grammarians allow it in any tense.
rows.anchor: مادهما والذراع من المرفق إلى رأس للأصبع الوسطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wasid means the cave's doorway or passage; reports from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Atiyya gloss it as the area in front, while others say threshold or its adjacent ground.
rows.anchor: بموضع الباب ومحل العبور من الكهف وأنشدوا

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr's reported gloss of wasid as ṣaʿid is judged unsound.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر وغيره عن ابن جبير أن الوصيد الصعيد وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: The dog lay at the entrance to guard the cave; another report says it slept on one ear as the youths turned and switched ears when they turned the other way.
rows.anchor: كما يشير إليه ما أخرجه ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج قال : باسط ذراعيه بالوصيد

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن حميد المكي
rows.claim: A report from Abd Allah ibn Humayd al-Makki says the dog lived by licking its forelegs, suggesting it did not sleep through the entire period.
rows.anchor: لكن أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عبد الله بن حميد المكي أنه جعل رزقه في لحس ذراعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittalaʿta means to come upon something by direct sight and inspection.
rows.anchor: لو عاينتهم وشاهدتهم وأصل الاطلاع الوقوف على الشيء بالمعاينة والمشاهدة

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب والأعمش
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab and al-Aʿmash read ittaṭlaʿ with a damma on wāw by analogy with a pronoun wāw before a still letter; Shayba and Abu Jaʿfar also transmit it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب والأعمش ( لو اطلعت ) بضم الواو تشبيها لها بواو الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawallayta means turning away and showing them one's back; fararan may be an emphatic verbal noun, stand for an omitted verb, describe one's state, or give the reason for retreating.
rows.anchor: أي لأعرضت بوجهك عنهم وأوليتهم كشحك ونصب ( فرارا ) إما على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear filling someone is a familiar metaphor for its intensity; ruʿban may be a second object or a specification converted from the subject.
rows.anchor: أي خوفا يملأ الصدر ونصب على أنه مفعول ثان ويجوز أن يكون تمييزا

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects deriving ruʿban from an object as in “the earth burst into springs,” since the verb here would otherwise govern a direct object.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أبعد من ذهب إلى أنه تمييز محول عن المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the cause of terror was the awe and majesty God cast upon the youths; others attribute it to long hair and nails, yellow faces, worn clothes, or a dark, desolate cave.
rows.anchor: وسبب ما ذكر أن الله عز وجل ألقى عليهم من الهيبة والجلال ما ألقى وقيل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the bodily-change and desolate-place explanations: the youths themselves did not recognize changes, the messenger noticed only altered landmarks, and the spacious cave was not desolate.
rows.anchor: وتعقب ذلك أبو حيان بأن القولين ليسا بشيء لأنهم لو كانوا بتلك الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defenders answer that people waking may not notice their changed condition; the messenger's ignorance does not rule out others noticing it, and he may initially have spoken before realizing the duration.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنهم لا يبعد عدم تيقظهم لحالهم فإن القائم من النوم قد يذهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another response addresses the Prophet: frightening changes and an eerie setting could have developed after the sleepers awoke and sent their messenger into town.
rows.anchor: وأيضا يجوز أن يكون هذا الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك الحال إنما حدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds these counterarguments weak; the best explanation is awe God placed on them, with any grown hair or nails not reaching a startling length.
rows.anchor: و لا يخفى على منصف ما في هذه الأجوبة فالذي ينبغي أن يعول عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators say God never altered their appearance at all, preserving a clear sign; if the address is to the Prophet, their terrifying appearance must have lasted until revelation.
rows.anchor: واختار بعض المفسرين أن الله تعالى لم يغير حالهم وهيئتهم أصلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that during a campaign with Muawiya near the Roman lands, Muawiya wanted to inspect the cave, but Ibn Abbas said God had barred it even to someone better than him, namely the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muawiya insisted and sent men inside; God sent a wind that drove them out of the cave.
rows.anchor: دخلوه بعث الله تعالى عليهم ريحا فأخرجتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Muawiya thought their condition had changed; another says he simply wanted to learn about them if possible.
rows.anchor: وقيل وكأن معاوية إنما لم يجر على مقتضى كلام ابن عباس
